title: Minturn Well Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Minturn wells have a 40-foot median depth, but records reach 990 feet. See yields, costs, risks and permit history near Minturn.
h1: What to Know About Wells in Minturn, Colorado
intro_html:
Buying or building near Minturn means dealing with mountain bedrock, limited well records and sharply different site conditions. Within 5 miles of Minturn, Colorado, DWR records show 158 permitted wells, but only 56 are recorded as constructed. The available records point to generally shallow wells with strong reported yields, while the deepest well reaches 990 feet.

That summary is useful for screening a property, not for guaranteeing water. A driller still needs to evaluate the exact lot, access, geology, casing and grout requirements, and the intended household use.

sections.heading: Minturn well depths vary with the mountain bedrock
sections.html:
The median reported well depth near Minturn is 40 feet. The middle half runs from 19 to 116 feet, and 67% of recorded depths are under 100 feet. Another 27% fall between 100 and 300 feet, while 3% are between 300 and 600 feet and 3% exceed 600 feet. The deepest record is 990 feet.

For a drilling bid, the 40-foot median is a useful starting point, not a promise. Fractured granite and gneiss can produce water through specific fractures, so a nearby shallow well does not rule out a deeper hole on your lot. Ask for a written allowance for additional footage, casing, grout and difficult access.

sections.heading: Reported well yields near Minturn are mostly usable, but records are limited
sections.html:
Only 14 wells report a pump yield, so the yield sample is much smaller than the permit count. In that group, the median is 15.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 12.0 to 80.0 gallons per minute. No reported wells are under 1 gallon per minute or between 1 and 5 gallons per minute. Forty-three percent report 5 to 15 gallons per minute, and 57% report more than 15 gallons per minute.

Those figures suggest a favorable result among the wells with testing information. They do not establish what an untested lot will make. Confirm the proposed well's permitted use, pump test results and storage design. Colorado exempt household-use wells also have a 35 gallon-per-minute pumping limit.

sections.heading: The shallow water levels do not prove a declining table
sections.html:
Ten wells report a static water level. The median depth to water is 8 feet, and the middle half is 7 to 40 feet. That is shallow compared with the full range of drilling depths, but it should not be read as a guarantee that water will stand near the surface on a new well.

The permit counts by decade do not show a water-level trend. Records include 1 permit from the 1960s, 31 from the 1980s, 24 from the 1990s, 39 from the 2000s, 26 from the 2010s and 16 from the 2020s. The newest permit year is 2022. For a purchase, request current static-level and production information from nearby owners when available.

sections.heading: Permit history reaches from Minturn to Red Cliff and Vail
sections.html:
Permit records near Minturn span several decades, with the largest listed decade being the 2000s at 39 permits. The records include domestic or household wells at 16%, stock wells at 2% and monitoring wells at 67%. No wells are listed for irrigation. That high monitoring share matters: the overall database is not a direct picture of private household wells.

The most active drillers named in the records are Authorized (Pe, Pg), with 38 wells, Golden Eagle Drilling Corporation (Shelton, Joe Wayne), with 12, and Steve Shelton Drilling, Inc. (Shelton, Steve), with 5. These names describe permit history, not a recommendation or guarantee of current availability.

sections.heading: A median-depth Minturn well pencils out at $8,600-$16,000 finished
sections.html:
Minturn drilling conditions are modeled as fractured mountain bedrock, including granite and gneiss. The typical drilling rate is $65-$100 per foot. At the 40-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $2,600-$4,000. A finished well, including pump, tank, trenching and electrical, is estimated at $8,600-$16,000.

The deepest recorded well is 990 feet, so the median-cost example should not be used as a fixed project price. A longer hole, difficult road access, extra casing or unexpected bedrock can change the bid. Get the drilling footage allowance and the included equipment in writing before comparing proposals.

sections.heading: Mine features, PFAS sites and septic layout deserve a close look
sections.html:
Within about 10 miles of Minturn, the map includes 5 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 90 historic mine features and 6 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. These mapped sites do not automatically mean a particular well is contaminated, but they justify checking the well location, drainage direction and available water-quality records.

Low yield and dry holes remain possible in fractured bedrock even when nearby records look good. Test water for the conditions relevant to the site and proposed use. Before building, confirm well separation from the septic system, room for the drainfield, winter access, electrical routing and equipment space. An augmentation plan may also matter in an over-appropriated basin.

sections.heading: Use nearby records to screen a Minturn lot before you buy
sections.html:
Start with the exact parcel and compare permitted wells near it, rather than relying on the overall Minturn median. Red Cliff is about 2 miles away, Vail 7 miles, Avon 10 miles and Copper Mountain 10 miles; Edwards is 14 miles away and Fulford 15 miles away. Those areas provide context, but geology and water conditions can change across short mountain distances.

For an existing home, verify the permit, construction record, pump equipment, static level and recent water test. For a vacant lot, make the well feasibility review part of due diligence before closing. Have a Colorado driller and septic professional assess access, siting and the likely depth range, then budget for a result that may differ from the local median.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Minturn, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within 5 miles of Minturn is 40 feet. The middle half ranges from 19 to 116 feet, and 67% are under 100 feet. Conditions still vary widely: 3% of reported depths exceed 600 feet, and the deepest record is 990 feet. Fractured mountain bedrock makes the exact lot more important than the median.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Minturn?
faq.a: The modeled drilling rate near Minturn is $65-$100 per foot. At the 40-foot median depth, the drilled hole is about $2,600-$4,000. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching and electrical is estimated at $8,600-$16,000. A 990-foot record shows why a buyer should ask about extra footage and difficult access before accepting a bid.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Minturn?
faq.a: Only 14 wells near Minturn report a pump yield. Their median is 15.0 gallons per minute, with the middle half from 12.0 to 80.0 gallons per minute. Forty-three percent report 5 to 15 gallons per minute and 57% report more than 15 gallons per minute. These results describe recorded tests, not a guarantee for a new well.

faq.q: Is well water safe to drink in Minturn?
faq.a: The available well records do not establish drinking-water safety. Within about 10 miles, there are 5 PFAS sampling or contamination sites, 90 historic mine features and 6 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. A buyer should test the individual well and review nearby site information, especially before using the water for household drinking and cooking.

faq.q: Are Minturn wells affected by low water levels?
faq.a: Ten wells report static water levels near Minturn. The median depth to water is 8 feet, with the middle half from 7 to 40 feet. The permit-by-decade series does not show a water-level trend because it counts permits rather than repeated measurements. Ask for current static-level information and a production test for the specific property.
